seed_note: Fixed seed (today's date, 2026-09-25) used for shuffling group_keys before split assignment. Re-running the generator (script preserved at artifacts/v2/../../ -- see docs/v2/PHASE4_BENCHMARK.md for the generation-script pointer) with this seed reproduces an identical split.
grouping_method: Every case carries a group_key, usually a drug/target/disease-family tag (e.g. 'family_osimertinib_egfr'). Cases about the same drug/entity family across different sources (e.g. a PubMed case, a ClinicalTrials case, a ChEMBL case, and a multi-source case all about tirzepatide) share one group_key so they are never split across development/validation/phase4_heldout -- this follows the same discipline as artifacts/v2/phase3_benchmark_manifest.json's grouping_method (group_key-based splitting, never splitting a group across splits). Because group sizes here are uneven (a multi-source drug family can hold up to 6 cases, a single-fact case is its own 1-case group), splitting is done by randomly shuffling the list of DISTINCT group_keys with the fixed seed above, then greedily assigning each group in that shuffled order to whichever of development/validation/phase4_heldout is currently furthest below its 60%/20%/20% CASE-count target -- this keeps the no-group-ever-split-across-splits guarantee while landing close to a 60/20/20 case-count split despite uneven group sizes (a plain group-count cut, as used unmodified, produced a skewed 37/18/6 split here and was rejected in favor of this case-count-aware variant).
gold_label_process: Every case's gold relevance judgment was produced by direct human (author) verification against a real, checkable source record -- never by asking an LLM 'is this relevant' and accepting the answer. Three verification methods were used, each recorded per-case in that case's `verification` field: (1) local_corpus_inspection -- for PubMed RAG cases, the actual title+abstract text of the candidate PMID was read directly out of data/corpus/abstracts.jsonl (the exact corpus retrieval/retriever.py indexes) to judge genuine topical relevance before labeling it gold; (2) live_pubmed_api / live_clinicaltrials_v2_api / live_chembl_api -- for cases needing content not in (or not confirmably in) the local corpus, and for all ClinicalTrials/ChEMBL cases (which have no local index per docs/v2/PHASE4_INITIAL_RETRIEVAL_AUDIT.md Sections B/C), the real public API was called during benchmark construction (2026-09-25) and the actual returned record (title, condition list, phase, status, pref_name, max_phase, mechanism fields) was read to judge relevance -- e.g. CHEMBL-COMPOUND-02's osimertinib ID: an initial guess (CHEMBL1743081) was checked live, found to actually be TRALOKINUMAB (an unrelated drug), and discarded before the correct ID (CHEMBL3353410) was found via a live name search -- a concrete record of rejecting a wrong guess rather than asserting it; (3) tool_signature_inspection / orchestration_models_inspection -- for abstention/unsupported-operation cases, the real tool method signatures (tools/pubmed_tool.py, tools/clinical_trials_tool.py, tools/chembl_tool.py) and typed argument schemas (orchestration/models.py) were read in full to confirm no operation exists to serve the query, rather than assuming. Two of ChEMBL's cases (CHEMBL-TARGET-02, CHEMBL-AMBIG-01, and NEG-AMBIG-COMPOUND-01) additionally document a real, live-observed WRONG_ENTITY failure mode (the tool's search_by_target first-hit heuristic returning an unrelated protein-protein-interaction or wrong-organism/wrong-gene record ahead of the correct target) -- this was discovered empirically during verification, not hypothesized in advance, and is recorded with the literal API response order as evidence.

phase2_consumed_test_split.note: Not read for case content or gold labels; this benchmark's query text is entirely new and does not reuse or paraphrase any Phase 2 benchmark item.

phase3_spent_heldout.note: phase3_benchmark_manifest.json was read ONLY to learn its case-format convention and grouping/split methodology (Section C of the governing directive explicitly permits this); no Phase 3 query text, group_key, or gold label was copied, reused, or paraphrased into this file. All 61 query strings in this file were newly authored for Phase 4 and independently checked against Phase 3's original_query strings for verbatim/near-verbatim overlap -- none found.

phase10_not_touched.note: Phase 10 does not exist yet in this repository (no docs/v2/PHASE10_*, no artifacts/v2/phase10_*) -- confirmed by directory listing; nothing under any Phase-10 name was read, created, or modified.

retrieval_contract_reference: docs/v2/PHASE4_RETRIEVAL_CONTRACT.md, artifacts/v2/phase4_retrieval_contract.json -- gold labels here are expressed against RetrievalCandidate.source_record_id (PMID | NCT ID | ChEMBL ID), never a fabricated identifier, per that contract's Section 3 source-specific contracts.
gate_plan_reference: docs/v2/PHASE4_GATE_PLAN.md -- category field values and expected_failure_category fields on individual cases map onto that document's Section 1 failure taxonomy (NO_RESULTS, RELEVANT_ITEM_MISSED, WRONG_ENTITY, WRONG_SOURCE, OVER_FILTERED, UNDER_FILTERED, STALE_INDEX, etc.); no new failure category was invented for this benchmark -- every expected_failure_category value used below already appears in that taxonomy.

cases.query: What ChEMBL compounds are being developed against the MET oncogene target for cancer treatment?

A short, ambiguous 3-letter gene symbol ('MET') is a realistic and severe case of the WRONG_ENTITY risk.

cases.gold_label_rationale: Most severe verified WRONG_ENTITY example found during construction: the tool's real first-hit heuristic returns a completely unrelated organism/protein (E. coli Met repressor) for a common short oncology gene symbol.

verification.evidence: GET .../target/search.json?q=MET&limit=6 returned, in order: target[0]=CHEMBL1938227 ('Met repressor', SINGLE PROTEIN, Escherichia coli -- an unrelated bacterial methionine-biosynthesis repressor, NOT the human oncogene), target[1]=CHEMBL4523234 ('Granzyme M' -- also wrong), target[2]=CHEMBL3717 ('Hepatocyte growth factor receptor', Homo sapiens -- the correct MET oncogene target) appearing only 3rd.
